chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, from Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of God upon him) who said:

Indeed, God — Blessed and Exalted — has purified us and protected us ('isma), and made us witnesses over His creatures, and His divine authority (hujja) in His earth, and made us [to be] with the Quran, and made the Quran [to be] with us — we do not separate from it, and it does not separate from us.

key_terms.الْقُرْآن: The Quran — the Imams are declared to be inseparable from it, reflecting the Thaqalayn tradition
key_terms.حُجَّتَهُ: His hujja — God's proof/authority on earth; a central concept in Shia theology for the role of the Imam
key_terms.شُهَدَاء: Witnesses — the Imams as divine witnesses over creation, a theological office
key_terms.طَهَّرَنَا: Purified us — referring to the divine purification (tahara) of the Ahlulbayt, as referenced in Quran 33:33
key_terms.عَصَمَنَا: 'Isma — infallibility, divine protection from sin and error; a theological cornerstone of the Imams' status

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the relationship between the Imams and the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) declares the unique theological status of the Imams of the Ahlulbayt: that God has bestowed upon them the qualities of purity (tahara) and infallibility ('isma), appointed them as witnesses over all of creation, and established them as His authoritative proofs (hujaj) on earth. Most significantly, he asserts the inseparable bond between the Imams and the Quran — a direct expression of the Hadith al-Thaqalayn doctrine that the Quran and the Ahlulbayt will never part from one another until the Day of Judgment. This hadith was transmitted through Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, one of the earliest companions who documented Ali's statements about Imamate.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, from Suleym Bin Qays Al Hilaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Purified us<sup>asws</sup>, and Protected us<sup>asws</sup>, and Made us<sup>asws</sup> witnesses upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Divine Authorities in His<sup>azwj</sup> earth, and Made us to be with the Quran, and Made the Quran to be with us<sup>asws</sup>. Neither will we<sup>asws</sup> separate from it, nor will it separate from us’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali from Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, cleansed us, granted us protection against sins, made us to bear witness to the activities of His creatures and granted us Divine authority on earth. He made us to be with the holy Quran and the Holy Quran to be with us. We do not depart the Holy Quran and the Holy Quran does not depart us.”
